regions.name: Bellingshausen Sea (Antarctica)
regions.why: The other pole of the Antarctic sea-ice dipole, west of the Antarctic Peninsula.

T2M.label: Air temperature
T2M.simple: How warm the air is 2 metres above the ground — what a thermometer in the shade shows.

TS.label: Surface temperature
TS.simple: The temperature of the surface itself — soil, rock, sea water or ice — which can be much hotter or colder than the air above it.

FRSEAICE.label: Sea ice cover
FRSEAICE.simple: The share of the ocean surface covered by floating sea ice: 0 % is open water, 100 % is fully frozen over.

SLP.label: Sea-level pressure
SLP.simple: The weight of the air above a spot, as if measured at sea level (about 1013 hPa on average): low pressure brings storms, high pressure fair weather.

WS10M.label: Wind speed
WS10M.simple: How fast the wind blows 10 metres above the ground (10 m/s is 36 km/h).

PRECTOTCORR.label: Precipitation
PRECTOTCORR.simple: How much rain and snow falls, in millimetres of water per day (1 mm on one square metre is one litre). MERRA-2 corrects its model rain with rain gauges and satellite observations.

TQV.label: Water vapour in the air column
TQV.simple: All the water vapour above a spot, from the ground to the top of the atmosphere — the millimetres of water you would get if it all rained out at once.

TROPT.label: Tropopause temperature
TROPT.simple: The temperature at the tropopause, the ceiling of the weather layer of the atmosphere: about 8 km up near the poles and 17 km up in the tropics.

links.text: Air temperature and Surface temperature leave their norm in the same months, the same way: 106 times, where chance at the same moment of the record would give 37 (p = 2e-34; z = 21.5 against the same reading with one of them moved 1 to 5 years, beyond the shared trend and the persistence of each). So often, both ways (76 % and 79 %), that Eva takes them for one dynamic seen through the identity: in 61 months one left its norm without the other.

Water vapour in the air column — Bellingshausen Sea (Antarctica): +0.07 kg/m² per decade (95 % range +0.00962 to +0.129). A rising trend that only one test (or only the 90 % level) supports. Mann-Kendall p = 0.024, t-test p = 0.05. With this much natural variability, a trend of this size needs about 59 years of data to stand out (45 so far). Model note: both series come from the MERRA-2 reanalysis, not from two independent instruments: confirm it with an independent dataset before calling it a finding.

story.text: Sea ice cover — Bellingshausen Sea (Antarctica): +0.28 % per decade (95 % range -0.8 to +1.23). A rising tendency that is not significant (yet): it could be chance. Mann-Kendall p = 0.55, t-test p = 0.79. With this much natural variability, a trend of this size needs about 173 years of data to stand out (45 so far). Eva: Since 2011, months come out above Eva's expectation 53 % of the time: not clearly different from her 1981–2010 norm.

Tropopause temperature — Bellingshausen Sea (Antarctica): +0.09 °C per decade (95 % range -0.0553 to +0.251). A rising tendency that is not significant (yet): it could be chance.
